📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • In a recent development, most of us have an understanding of what it means to be stressed.
  • Sources indicate that there are some general patterns to the way stress affects us.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

In a recent development, most of us have an understanding of what it means to be stressed. We’ve all experienced the physical, cognitive, and emotional changes that stress can produce. In general, stress represents our physical and mental response to challenge, change, or threat. That response is different among individuals, changes over time, depending on what we’ve learned about how to handle challenges, our physical health, and even how tired we might be when we encounter a stressful event.

Sources indicate that there are some general patterns to the way stress affects us. One pattern is that stress early in life can, in some individuals, change the response to later stress. The stress sensitization hypothesis proposes that early exposure to stressful events can amplify our later response to stress, making us more vulnerable to psychological distress like depression and anxiety (Stroud, 2018).

The stress sensitization hypothesis grew out of research by Robert Post in the early 1990s. Post noted that stressful events tended to be associated more with “the first episode of major affective disorder than with subsequent episodes” (p. 999). These first stressors sensitized our nervous system, changing the way that the genes for neurotransmitters and receptors are expressed, which in turn changes the ways in which neurons respond, ultimately changing our responses to the next stressful event. He proposed that these long-term changes in neural systems can lead to “stress sensitization,” or the risk that even very low-intensity stress events can trigger episodes of depression after the first stress exposure, and “stress autonomy,” where episodes of depression can occur even without the stressful event being present (Post 1992, Stroud, 2018).

In a recent development, the physical changes that characterize the stress response are collectively referred to as the “fight or flight response” (FFR). The FFR begins with activation of the sympathetic adrenal medullary (SAM) system, called the “fast” system because it is activated immediately, which ultimately tells the adrenal gland to release norepinephrine and epinephrine (adrenaline). SAM system activation increases muscle tension, respiration, and heart rate, as well as cognitive/behavioral changes like increased arousal, alertness, vigilance, and analgesia. The slower hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) system is also activated by a signal from the amygdala, ultimately telling the adrenal gland to release the hormone cortisol, which signals the liver to release glucose and fatty acids to fuel the body’s response to the threat (Chus, Marwaha, Sanvictores, Awosika and Ayers, 2024).

Sources indicate that short-term stress that can be resolved relatively quickly can enhance learning and memory, but long-term, chronic stress produces negative effects on both body and cognition. Essentially, all of the physical and psychological aspects of the stress response that help us handle stress in the short term can, if the stress continues without letting up, become maladaptive (Schwabe and Daskalakis, 2025). Part of that maladaptive response to long-term stress is the potential for an increased risk of depression and anxiety.

Sources indicate that stroud (2018) points out that about half of the people who experience one episode of depression do not go on to experience another episode, despite the fact that they have undoubtedly experienced subsequent major and minor stresses in life. Individuals also vary in resilience to stress and its effects. A complex array of genetic, social, environmental, and learned factors makes some individuals more resilient to stress than others.

Investigations into what makes people resistant to the effects of stress have centered on the SAM and HPA systems. In a review of the research into stress resilience, Ozbay, Johnson, Dimoulas, Morgan, Charney and Southwick (2007) note that “stress resilience seems to be associated with an ability to keep the HPA-axis and SAM system activity within an optimal range during stress exposure and terminate the stress response once the stressor is no longer present” (p. 36). Research into neural control of these two systems has focused on the role of the hypothalamus, which sits at the beginning of both the fast and slow systems.

Sources indicate that using a mouse model of stress, Pennington, LaBanca, Mahmud, et al. (2026) investigated the role of the anterior hypothalamus (AH) in creating stress sensitivity and the effects of the neural changes stress induces. Mice in group 1 were exposed to a high-intensity stressor (foot shock). Group 2 mice were not stressed at all. Ten days later, both groups of mice were exposed to a new, novel potential stressor (a sound they had not heard before), and their “freeze” response (the typical mouse response to something new and threatening) to this mild stress was assessed. Previously shocked mice froze for a significantly longer period of time than did non-shocked mice, indicating increased stress sensitivity in the shocked group. A scan of a marker for neural activity (c-fos) in the brains of these two groups of mice demonstrated much higher activity in the hypothalamus of group 1 mice after exposure to the sound than in group 2 mice. This hyper-reactivity was particularly marked in the AH.

Recordings of activity in the AH neurons revealed that they responded specifically to negative, aversive stimuli and were inhibited by rewards. In addition, exposure to prior stress amplified the proportion of AH neurons that responded to negative stimuli, evidence of probable stress sensitization.

It appears that previous exposure to stress can reorganize the way the brain responds to subsequent stressful stimuli, via the AH. A better understanding of how the brain reacts to stress may help find ways to increase stress resilience and to decrease sensitivity to early stressors.

US battery storage just topped 200 GWh – here’s where it is

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
  • Sources indicate that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • Recent findings suggest that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

Sources indicate that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

Recent findings suggest that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

Sources indicate that utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of new capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

Sources indicate that “States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” noted Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, Fresh York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

It has been revealed that the US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

Recent findings suggest that you wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

The article is good with the reporting about grid tied storage, but seems to miss the forest for the trees with it comes to pricing. Texas isn't installing more grid tied storage because of altruistic intent.

Sources indicate that the storage is being added because they electricity suppliers can use it to make money. They can make money because we have a reasonably well thought out wholesale electrical market AND because that market has purchases large amounts of solar and wind generation.

According to recent reports, that combination means that I still pay just $0.01 more per kwh than I did when I moved to this state 20 years ago. I pay 12 cents per kwh and Texas average is between 12 and 15. A functional market is what makes that work.

It has been revealed that more than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty notes the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

Latest Update: High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Reveals

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a new study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.
  • The researchers from Arizona State University remarked a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.
  • The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a new study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.

The researchers from Arizona State University remarked a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.

The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.

The researchers published their findings on November 12 in the journal Stem Cell Reports.

Industry observers note that the researchers noted the study is important because 1 in 25 people develop colon cancer in their lifetime. In the United States, that translates into about 108,000 new cases of colon cancer every year. About 55,000 males and 55,000 females are expected to die from the disease in 2026.

Experts not involved in the study say the research provides valuable information, but they have reservations about the results, as the findings do not yet apply to humans.

“The findings provide a potential mechanism linking diet to intestinal cancer development, but we need to be cautious about translating these results to humans,” noted Dalia Perelman, MS, CDE, a research dietitian at Stanford University in California.

“We already have evidence from human studies that obesity and certain dietary patterns, particularly those high in processed meats and low in fiber-rich foods, are associated with increased colorectal cancer risk,” Perelman told Healthline. “This study adds a potentially important mechanism to investigate, but it does not establish that dietary fat itself increases colorectal cancer risk in humans.”.

Ketan Thanki, MD, a colorectal surgeon specializing in benign and malignant diseases of the colon, rectum, and anus at the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in California, shared similar views.

“This study provides a better understanding at the cellular level of how a high fat diet may contribute to colorectal cancer development,” Thanki told Healthline.

Industry observers note that “Animal studies are an important starting point for understanding biological processes, but we must be cautious about directly applying their findings to humans,” he added. “Mice and humans share many cellular and biological mechanisms, which makes these studies valuable in identifying potential pathways involved in disease development. However, human diets, genetics, metabolism, and environmental exposures are more complex.”.

To reach their findings, the Arizona State researchers fed mice what the scientists described as a Western-style high fat diet for 6 months.

They then compared those results with those from mice given a low fat diet.

According to recent reports, the researchers remarked the mice on the high fat diet gained more weight than the mice on the low-fat diet. They also developed more intestinal stem cells, and those cells grew at a more rapid rate.

They added that mice genetically predisposed to intestinal cancer who were fed a high-fat diet developed more and larger tumors.

The researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may help explain their increased growth and survival.

It has been revealed that they also pointed out that stem cell behavior returned to normal after high fat diet mice were switched to a low fat diet, although some DNA changes persisted. After four weeks, approximately 18% of these changes remained.

When mice were returned to a high fat diet, the researchers noted their intestinal stem cells responded more quickly and strongly than those of mice exposed to the diet for the first time.

They concluded that the study suggests that maintaining a healthy, low fat diet may help regulate intestinal stem cell growth and reduce colon cancer risk.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, RD, president of KAK Consulting and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine in Ohio, wasn’t involved in the study but highlighted a particular aspect of the findings.

According to recent reports, “What I found particularly interesting was that even after the mice returned to a low fat diet, some of the molecular changes persisted,” she told Healthline. “This raises questions about how our dietary patterns over time may influence long-term health.”.

Experts mentioned these fresh findings are interesting but noted numerous caveats.

According to recent reports, “One important takeaway is that dietary habits over time matter,” mentioned Thanki. “Even if someone has consumed a high fat diet for years, making changes now may still provide meaningful health benefits.”.

“I also think these findings are particularly key for children and adolescents, as establishing healthier dietary habits early in life may provide long-term benefits,” he added.

It has been revealed that however, Thanki noted that not all fats are the same. “The health risks depend partly on the type of fat consumed, how much is consumed, and what foods make up the overall diet,” he said.

“Diets consistently high in saturated fats, particularly those containing large amounts of processed meats, fried foods, and highly processed products, can contribute to obesity, elevated cholesterol, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. These factors can also contribute to chronic inflammation and may increase the risk of certain cancers, including colorectal cancer,” Thanki continued.

Perelman said the diet used in the study was extremely high in fat, providing 60% of calories from fat, primarily from lard.

“We know that the health effects of dietary fats differ depending on their sources and fatty acid composition, and we cannot assume that a diet rich in unsaturated fats from foods such as olive oil, nuts, and seeds would produce the same effects,” she noted.

Perelman added that the researchers primarily studied stem cells from the small intestine rather than the colon.

“Although these tissues share some biological characteristics, they have vital differences, and we cannot assume that the same changes would occur in the colon,” she explained.

Finally, Perelman noted that “the mice consuming the high fat diet also gained weight, making it difficult to separate the effects of dietary fat itself from those associated with increased body fat and other metabolic changes.”.

Not all high fat foods are unhealthy. Some high fat foods that offer healthy benefits include:.

Sources indicate that “The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to eliminate fat because our bodies need healthy fats for normal functioning,” mentioned Thanki. “Instead, people should focus on reducing saturated and trans fats while incorporating healthier unsaturated fats in appropriate amounts.”.

Sources indicate that thanki had several dietary suggestions. Among them:.

Industry observers note that “Consistency matters more than perfection. Even modest dietary changes, maintained over time, can have meaningful health benefits,” Thanki said.

Sources indicate that perelman agreed. “The overall quality of the diet matters. Diets that are very high in fat may displace other foods and nutrients that have key health benefits,” she said.

“For colorectal cancer specifically, higher intakes of dietary fiber and whole grains have consistently been associated with lower risk,” Perelman noted.

“Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on reducing fat, it is crucial to consider the overall dietary pattern and whether it provides adequate amounts of fiber-rich plant foods and other beneficial nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick agreed that the type of fat is what is vital. “A Mediterranean-style diet that includes olive oil, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish can be relatively high in fat but is consistently associated with positive health outcomes,” she noted.

“On the other hand, a diet high in saturated fat, processed meats, and ultra-processed foods may increase the risk of certain chronic diseases, particularly when it’s also low in fiber and other protective nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick also noted that many lifestyle habits contribute to a person’s overall health.

“Our health is influenced by so many factors beyond diet, including how we manage stress, our sleep habits, physical activity, genetics, and overall lifestyle,” she stated.

The Hyundai Elantra continues to defy the apparent incipient death of the sedan, and the Korean automaker just gave it a major upgrade for 2027. Between a latest “Art of Steel” design, a larger size, and upgraded infotainment technology, the 2027 Hyundai Elantra is more prepared for the future than ever before.

Recent findings suggest that revealed Thursday at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show, the 2027 Elantra's most obvious feature is its exterior design. Created under Hyundai's new Art of Steel design philosophy, which was first revealed on the Boulder concept, the Elantra is now a boxy beast with wide fenders, sharp headlights, and a square rear end. This new sedan was designed with a very clear three-box configuration and sport sedan dynamism in mind, according to Hyundai’s head of design.

It has been revealed that “There is an inherent beauty in a sedan because its proportions are honest, intuitive and functional,” stated SangYup Lee, executive vice president and head of the Hyundai and Genesis Global Design Center. “With the all-newly introduced Elantra, we returned to that essence, then pushed it forward. Wide, muscular fenders, a long hood, and refined three-box proportions give Elantra a confident, athletic presence that challenges the conventions of the compact sedan.”.

In addition to the latest exterior design, changes under the skin mean the latest Elantra is now 3.3 inches longer, 1.1 inches wider, and features a 1.1-inch longer wheelbase than its predecessor; all told, Hyundai indicates the 2027 Elantra has over one inch more rear headroom and legroom. So-called H-Edge lighting, futuristic grille styling, slim- neck mirrors, and lift-up flush door handles make up the rest of the visual changes.

In a recent development, but Hyundai didn’t stop its design renovations with the exterior. Inside the Elantra, the carmaker added a newly introduced Curve of Upholstery design and an asymmetrical front layout, which is meant to “gently embrace” the driver. A central 12.9-inch Pleos Connect infotainment system is standard on all Elantra models, while an available slim information display in the driver’s natural line of sight provides critical driving information. Other interior features include 15-kW dual wireless phone charging, Audio by Bang & Olufsen, Hyundai Digital Key 2, and 100-watt ultra-fast charging USB ports. Upholstery will be available in four black color combinations, as well as Burgundy/Rose Ivory and Chalk Beige.

Mechanically, the Elantra is a bit less exciting. The new model will offer two powertrain options: a 1.6-liter hybrid four-cylinder powerplant, and a naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine. The hybrid model will deliver 154 horsepower through a six-speed dual-clutch transmission, while the purely internal combustion model offers 146 horsepower routed through a continuously variable transmission. Hybridized Elantra models also feature a predictive drive system that intelligently anticipates driving patterns and road conditions to maximize efficiency, as well as a new “Stay Mode” that lets the climate control, stereo, charging ports and other non-motion-related functions operate for up to 30 minutes with the engine off.

Sources indicate that the pure ICE version will arrive as a 2027 model year Elantra, while the new Hyundai Elantra Hybrid will debut as a 2028 model year vehicle. Specific on-sale timing, pricing, fuel economy ratings and other details will be revealed closer to the vehicle’s American launch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

In a recent development, the game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

According to recent reports, battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Industry observers note that given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

Breaking: Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates.
  • “We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement.
  • Even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates. In a study published today in the journal npj Microgravity, botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) proved it’s possible to grow healthy, edible potatoes in simulated moon soil with the help of everyday worms. Importantly, the team also identified the proper proportions of lunar regolith and compost needed to produce potato yields similar to those grown on Earth.

“We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement. “That’s an key step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.”.

Even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts. They’ll require carefully maintained, nutritious diets to keep them healthy, but it’s not as simple as sending them off packed with calorically dense prepackaged meals. Cargo room on spacecraft is limited and costly, and the desolate lunar surface isn’t exactly hospitable to agriculture. In addition to constant bombardment by cosmic and solar radiation, temperatures can swing anywhere between 250 degrees and -410 degrees Fahrenheit.

Indoor horticulture will also be challenging. Lunar regolith is an annoyingly powdery substance composed of sharp-edged, miniscule particles created over billions of years of asteroid impacts, but little else. With essentially no organic material at all, the dust alone isn’t capable of supporting plant life.

Recent findings suggest that while it is easy enough to combine that lunar regolith with agricultural additives, researchers weren’t sure if these could overcome moon soil’s heavy metals and irradiation. To test it, Goyer and his colleagues first obtained simulated lunar regolith made to resemble the samples collected during the Apollo missions. Regolith composition varies by region on the moon, so they selected five different types based on darker lunar mare dust and the lighter lunar highland soil. They then mixed the mock moon dust with vermicompost, the nutrient-rich soil created when worms break down organic materials. Next, they planted potatoes in various ratios of regolith and vermicompost, and monitored their growth. As a control, the team even planted potatoes in soil taken from Hermiston, Oregon, an area famous for some of the world’s highest spud yields.

Industry observers note that the team found that composite soil with only 30 percent vermicompost was enough to produce potato crops comparable to those farmed on Earth. Their findings suggest the supplemental organics bind to the regolith’s heavy metals, which shield the plants and minimize any damage to their roots.

“We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith,” added OSU botanist and study co-author David Handy.

According to recent reports, but bushels of moon potatoes only go so far if they lack any real nutritional value. Even here, the lunar simulations offered promising results, particularly when it came to glycoalkaloids. The naturally forming potato toxins can cause green skin discoloration, but analysis indicated no statistically relevant rise in glycoalkaloids for the lunar crops.

With the potato viability debate settled, Goyer’s team will next compare 10 specific spud varieties grown in simulated lunar regolith to determine the most nutritious and resilient options for NASA astronomers.

Tech Report: How to Deal With a Significant Liar

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • According to recent reports, sure, it's common to encounter little lies that don't matter a whole lot in the grand scheme of things—like being told you look great in an outfit when you actually look like Bubble Bass from SpongeBob SquarePants.
  • Sources indicate that this can occur, for example, when someone without the proper credentials or track record is trying to get ahead in an area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

According to recent reports, sure, it's common to encounter little lies that don't matter a whole lot in the grand scheme of things—like being told you look great in an outfit when you actually look like Bubble Bass from SpongeBob SquarePants. But it can be a different story when you run into a significant liar—someone willing to completely fabricate things about you in order to discredit or take something away from you. One cannot lie. This can be quite a frustrating experience.

Sources indicate that this can occur, for example, when someone without the proper credentials or track record is trying to get ahead in an area. If you are already well-established in that area, you may promptly become a target of liars using big lies to take your ideas, credit, or resources. This can even include liars accusing you of doing what they are trying to do themselves—namely taking something from them when they actually took it from you.

That's the opposite of a gas. It's gaslighting, which I've covered before for "A Funny Bone to Pick." It can leave you questioning reality, as in, "Hold on a second. Someone who has no experience in my area of expertise is somehow claiming that I took an idea from that person?".

And people who've already demonstrated that they have no qualms about lying may stop at nothing to get what they want. Such dangerous people may try to bury you in a flurry of fabrications. So what can you do?

The very first thing is to gain control of the situation and completely cut off any interactions with the liar that are not clearly documentable. Substantial liars will use such undocumented meetings to trap you and generate more fodder for more lies—like claiming you behaved in such-and-such manner or mentioned such-and-such during the meeting. It can then become a you-said-liar-said situation. And guess who then has the upper hand if you aren't willing to lie but the liar certainly is?

Sources indicate that and don't get trapped in meetings that have so-called witnesses who have been chosen and set up by the liar to go against you. You never know what control the liar may have over others—such as pictures of others in some kind of compromising position with fish—that may force the witnesses to lie, too. So, choose your witnesses carefully yourself and maybe record the meeting as a backup.

Sources indicate that documentation is so key because liars can be notoriously slippery—using lots of undocumented side conversations with others to spread falsehoods. Liars operate best in the dark—sort of like vampires. And what's the best way to combat vampires? Sunlight.

Sources indicate that yes, your goal should be to get the liar and the liar's actions out in the open as soon as possible for everyone to see. One way is to switch all your conversations to email while telling everyone clearly why you are doing so. In fact, try asking the liar direct questions by email. Anyone with nothing to hide should be able to answer such questions directly, right? Any hedging or reluctance can suggest otherwise.

This may seem like a lot of work, especially when no one else around you seems to care about the truth at the moment. Liars, by definition, typically don't play the long game—because they otherwise might see the long-term consequences of lying and how it may catch up to them eventually. Lying to them seems like an easy short-term fix. But if you play the long game and keep noting every lie, you never know when it may come in handy down the road.

Industry observers note that since liars frequently will use lies to pit other people against you, don't take on a liar by yourself. The sooner you document the lies and show them to others—including those in the legal profession—the better. If the liar somehow thinks that you are alone, isolated, and thus easy to bully, you may have to flex your network to the liar a bit.

According to recent reports, it can help to expand the so-called blast radius of any of the liar's actions. When a liar drops a lie, bring others into the conversation. That will force the liar to lie to more and more people.

It has been revealed that all the while, be mindful of any role switching that big liars may do—such as playing the victim when they are the ones actually attacking you. Liars can be great actors because they aren't hampered by inconvenient stuff like truth, evidence, and facts.

So, stay cool, and stick to the facts. Don't play their game and resort to vague, unsupported statements. Significant liars are going to be better at that than you.

Recent findings suggest that throughout the downpour of lies, choose what you do and don't care to fight, practice self-care, and get support from your friends. The gaslighting can be tough and leave you wondering why others can't see what the big liar is doing and questioning humanity in general. Remember, though, that even if others do in fact see through the big liar, they may keep quiet because they don't want to get involved and may even fear the big liar themselves. Your good friends can provide healthy contrasts to such cowardly people.

It has been revealed that plus, ask yourself: Would you ever want to be the big liar? Such people have to rely on lying because they can't stand on their own merits. These are deep down insecure and broken people who have to keep maintaining increasingly tangled webs of lies. They've probably done the same lying to many other people, and at some point, it may all catch up to them.

Therefore, when it seems like the significant liar is getting away with something, ask yourself specifically what. Ultimately, these big liars can't get away from themselves and the sad existence of having to rely on lying. There's no lying about that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, toyota has had incredible success with pickup trucks in the United States of America. The Tacoma has become one of America’s perennial best-selling vehicles, while the Tundra has carved out a sustainable niche in America’s grueling full-size segment. But there’s arguably room for more.

In a recent development, rumors have long suggested Toyota is working on a compact, Ford Maverick-fighting pickup that would fill the truck lineup’s glaring need for a cheaper and more efficient option. Dealers have reportedly been asking Toyota for a compact pickup for several years. Mark Templin, Toyota’s COO in the United States, confirmed Toyota is “looking at” bringing a smaller pickup to the U.S. back in May 2025. And now, Toyota has just unveiled a newly introduced pickup that could fit that bill … for Latin American and Caribbean markets.

Toyota revealed a fresh compact pickup called the Corolla Cross Deck on Wednesday during its inauguration of a new production facility in Sococaba, Brazil, and it will enter production in the first half of 2027. According to Motor1 Brazil, the Corolla Cross Deck shares a TNGA-C platform with the Corolla sedan and Corolla Cross SUV. Toyota did not provide full specs, but did reveal a hybrid version—likely featuring the 1.8-liter 122-horsepower powertrain Toyota uses for the Corolla Cross in that market.

Industry observers note that sadly, Toyota has not confirmed potential availability for the Corolla Cross Deck in the American market. The automaker did not respond to a Road & Track inquiry about its potential availability by the time of publication, but we’ll enhancement this story if we receive a response.

According to recent reports, on paper, a Corolla-based compact pickup would likely be the easiest route for Toyota to bring a small, cheap pickup to the United States in the foreseeable future. Toyota already builds the Corolla and Corolla Cross at its Mazda Toyota Manufacturing Facility in Alabama; a new truck truck could be built on the same line—and even spawn potential rebadged variants for Toyota partners Mazda and Subaru.

Industry observers note that in the American market, the Toyota Corolla Cross uses 2.0-liter gas and hybrid engines. That powertrain could give Toyota options for a 169-horsepower base gas model truck—potentially starting below $30,000—and a 196-hp hybrid version that could eclipse 40 miles per gallon.

That stated, one could also see Toyota needing a different small truck approach to resonate with an American audience. One of Ford’s great innovations with the Maverick was that it looks more like the F-150 and Ranger than the Escape crossover it shared a platform with. And even if a newly introduced Toyota pickup were to share its bones with the Corolla, Toyota may want to brand it as an extension of the pickup line, rather than the Corolla family.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1080 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home.
  • The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran.
  • “While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” noted IEA executive director Fatih Birol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) new “World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.

The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran. Well-stocked oil inventories helped buffer the initial shock, and the IEA coordinated a release of emergency oil reserves. Some Gulf oil took routes around the strait. Atlantic Basin exporters shipped more, and China sharply cut its crude imports. Now more of the burden is falling on consumers, who are paying higher prices and cutting back.

“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” noted IEA executive director Fatih Birol.

It has been revealed that the IEA has seen EV sales jump in some countries hit by the crisis, along with increased trade in solar panels and batteries. For countries that import a lot of oil and gas, switching to EVs and heat pumps can help reduce their exposure to the next fuel price spike.

Industry observers note that “The impact of Hormuz is only just beginning to become clear,” said energy think tank Ember’s chief analyst Dave Jones. “Hormuz will speed up electrification and renewables, likely faster than many people think. So much of the momentum for electrification at COP31 comes from the desire to have cheaper and more secure energy.”.

Solar leads renewables growth in every scenario the IEA models, and nuclear power is growing strongly, too. Energy efficiency and biofuels could also gain ground. The push to use more homegrown energy could have a very different effect in parts of Asia, where some countries that import oil and gas have plenty of their own coal and could keep burning it for longer.

Sources indicate that the world was already using a lot more electricity before the crisis. Since 2019, electricity demand has grown twice as fast as overall energy demand, outpacing global economic growth. Everything from industrial motors and air conditioners to EVs, heat pumps, and data centers is driving that growth. Electricity comes close to 30% of the energy the world actually uses by 2035 in each of the IEA’s exploratory scenarios.

Recent findings suggest that before the crisis, around 20 million barrels of oil a day moved through the Strait of Hormuz. If shipping stays risky, new pipelines could route some of those barrels around the strait, while buyers turn to other suppliers or use less oil. In that case, the IEA claims the amount of oil that needs to pass through Hormuz could drop to 8.5 million barrels a day in 2030 and below 2 million by 2035. The Middle East would still be the world’s largest oil-exporting region.

If the conflict is resolved, oil and gas supply could bounce back. A delayed wave of liquefied natural gas could also help bring prices down even as buyers refill their inventories. Faster electrification could take some of the demand out of both markets.

Industry observers note that the world is now using more energy to cool its buildings than to heat them for the first time, the IEA says. By 2035, the global population is expected to grow by 650 million and the economy by a third. Energy needs rise gradually in advanced economies, growth slows in China, and India and Southeast Asia lead faster increases across other emerging and developing economies.

Then there’s AI. Under the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, global data center electricity use doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030. That buildout is already running into grid and supply chain constraints, and in some places, local opposition. The IEA also flags risks to critical mineral supplies and threats to energy infrastructure from natural hazards and cyberattacks.

Energy-related CO2 emissions stay around today’s levels under current policies. They start to fall under stated policies and drop further in the IEA’s Additional Response Case, which looks at what could happen if governments respond more strongly to the crisis. Even those deeper cuts fall short of what climate goals require. The current and stated policy scenarios point to 2.5C to 2.9C of warming, and the latest round of national climate pledges demonstrates little sign that countries are speeding up energy-sector emissions cuts.

Sources indicate that the green agenda always come in a second place because people cannot see that far out in the future. Stability of the economy and energy independence are much more notable drivers and have immediate impact. Local environment boosts like clean air in cities are also immediate drivers while long term reduced medical bills are not. The oil industry is challenged becuase, unlike previous numerous crises, there is an alternative and the green is the latest black.

There’s a more immediate cost, too. More people gained access to electricity and clean cooking in 2025, but higher fuel prices and shortages threaten to slow that progress. Around 720 million people still live without electricity, and nearly 2 billion cook with polluting fuels or technologies.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

In a recent development, black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#121055. Breaking: How Kelly Rowland Keeps Her Eczema Flare-Ups Under Control During Winter

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1106 w)

Breaking: How Kelly Rowland Keeps Her Eczema Flare-Ups Under Control During Winter

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight.
  • That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s.
  • “[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight. But for those with eczema, this time of year can wreak havoc on their skin, too.

That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s. During the winter months, she often dreads the cold.

“[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.

Cold weather and indoor heating can reduce humidity, drying out the skin and triggering or worsening eczema flare-ups.

“[What we know] about the skin barrier is that it really is like a gate or wall against the outside world,” Camille Howard-Verovic, MD, a dermatologist at Active Dermatology, told Healthline.

In a recent development, in healthy skin, the barrier controls what enters and leaves the skin. However, for people with eczema, Howard-Verovic mentioned they have skin barrier dysfunction, which allows substances such as allergens and irritants to penetrate the skin.

Cold weather can increase transepidermal water loss, a process in which moisture escapes through the skin’s outer barrier and evaporates into the surrounding air.

Industry observers note that “People with eczema have a tremendous amount of transepidermal water loss, so you’re just drier,” said Howard-Verovic. “[You’re] not holding onto the water as well, so that causes the itching and the rash that we feel when we have eczema.”.

Rowland first noticed eczema flares behind her ears as well as on her elbows, arms, and the back of her knees.

“[It] looked like a rash, so that’s what I thought it was all this time, and I dealt with it for so long until after I had my son and then it started to get worse on my face,” she mentioned.

She eventually went to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with moderate-to-severe eczema, a chronic inflammatory skin condition that can cause intense itching, painful skin cracking, thickened skin, and redness or swelling.

When Rowland learned that eczema can be genetic, it made sense to her.

“I remember seeing substantial rashes on [my mom’s] neck and her arms…so she had it, and I guess I was the lucky one,” stated Rowland.

At first, she tried eliminating foods that she thought might be triggers. She also bathed in oatmeal.

“[I] literally have had a tub full of oatmeal, like literally went to the store to get store-bought fresh oats,” she said. “I tried everything, and it doesn’t help until you go talk to a doctor about it.”.

At first, she tried prescription topical medications but found them cumbersome.

“I don’t have the time, if I’m being honest, and we live in a world that is moving so fast…I started buying like three tubes of whatever it was I was using and losing it; it was just too much for me,” Rowland mentioned.

Industry observers note that rowland remarked she found relief with Ebglyss, a prescription injectable medication for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. She has also partnered with Eli Lilly and Tech giant, its manufacturer, to raise awareness about eczema.

Rowland said she’s sharing her experience to help others living with eczema, including people she’s met who have experienced greater challenges managing the condition.

“One lady was telling me about how she’s having a tough time [looking] in the mirror cause she doesn’t know who’s looking back at her, and she saw her skin before eczema and after,” stated Rowland.

When she first had symptoms, she noted she felt embarrassed, too.

“[Because] it was just in the middle of my arm space and…[if I] put out my hand to shake someone’s hand, you don’t know if somebody’s judgy,” she stated.

Rowland hopes being open about her condition will encourage others to advocate for themselves and talk with their doctor about treatment options.

Because eczema can look different on deeper skin tones, Howard-Verovic noted that a dermatologist can help make the correct diagnosis.

It has been revealed that “Some people may not even know that they have eczema,” she remarked. “We know that eczema is a rash; it can appear red on certain skin tones, and it can be grey or white on certain skin tones, so it can look a little different.”.

In addition to medication, Rowland said managing stress helps reduce her eczema flare-ups.

According to recent reports, “Before [when] I went on tour, because I was under so much stress, it flared up like crazy, like you wouldn’t believe,” she said. “We were in the back trying to figure out how to cover certain things up, and we figured some of it out, and some of it was really tricky, but what helped was when I actually just calmed down…not that it helped overnight, but it did just kind of bring the flare down.”.

She remarked red light therapy, feeling grounded outside without her shoes on, getting vitamin D from natural sunlight, and cooking are ways she reduces ongoing stress.

“Cooking calms me when my kids aren’t here, and I have a really good [Zen] playlist on,” said Rowland. “[If] you ask me a question [in those moments], I might give you my heart; I’m just so happy.”.

She also tries to cut back on sugar, which she believes triggers flares.

Another way to reduce flares, according to Howard-Verovic, is to avoid hot showers, especially in the winter.

“[We] know eczematous skin likes lukewarm water,” she said.

Because Howard-Verovic and her daughter both live with eczema, she set a rule about when it’s time to get out of the shower.

It has been revealed that “[If] you see condensation on the bathroom mirror, you’ve spent too much time in the shower,” remarked Howard-Verovic. “[That] really hot, hot water feels really good in that moment…but when you get out all that water evaporates, and there’s no moisture in the atmosphere, and it dries your skin out, and now your skin is unhappy again.”.

If you prefer to take baths, she said use gentle cleansers.

“[There] are bleach baths for really, really bad flare-ups,” she noted.

Diluted bleach baths are sometimes recommended for people with eczema, but they should only be used according to a healthcare professional’s instructions.

According to recent reports, as soon as you get out of the shower or bath, Howard-Verovic remarked to apply a quality moisturizer to your damp skin. According to the National Eczema Association (NEA), lotions containing the following ingredients can help ease dry skin associated with eczema.

To help identify appropriate products, look for ones that have the NEA’s Seal of Acceptance.

Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.

Nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup. It looks fantastic as both a coupe and as a convertible. The active rear spoiler manages to maintain the sports car’s sleek profile whether it’s engaged or not, and the low nose with a thin, sweeping grille is classic Ferrari. The 296 drives as good as it looks, too, thanks to its hybrid powertrain that uses a twin-turbo V-6 engine.

Industry observers note that the Miata has been an enthusiast staple since it entered the market wide-eyed and grinning in 1990. It’s a head-turner in any generation, but the newest ND is the sportiest model yet, and it’s best enjoyed with the top down. We also love the look of the Retractable Fastback (RF) body style pictured here. For an incredibly fun and affordable sports car, the Miata is truly always the answer.

More About the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

Thin, sweeping taillights punctuate the nicely shaped rear end, while the classic diamond-shaped grille integrates beautifully with the slim, low-profile headlights. The G90 looks, sounds, and feels silky, and its sub-$100,000 starting price tag is surprising given how special it is.

Sources indicate that like the G90, the GV70’s sophisticated design language helps it punch above its weight against the Porsches and Mercedes-Benzes in its segment. Since then, it’s only gotten better thanks to a styling refresh for 2027. With a cheerfully aggressive front end and a sloped, sleek rear that tapers nicely, the GranTurismo coupe exudes high-performance fun in a stylish two-door package.

More About the Maserati GranTurismo.

The hotel staff immediately recognized the dog, but not because of her sparkling personality or floppy ears. Becky’s owner has dementia, and the unnamed man has disappeared before.

Recent findings suggest that the team at Whiteface called the Newly introduced York State Police (NYSP), who contacted the Department of Conservation (DEC) Forest Rangers for assistance with the search. Four NYSP officers and 14 Rangers used drones and another dog (a bloodhound) to search for the missing person. According to Charlie Foutch, the lead Ranger on the search, it was about 25 to 30 degrees Fahrenheit overnight.

At 10 a.m. the next morning, a hunter who was searching just ahead of the group heard someone fall and scream. He found the missing man off to the side of a trail in a draining area with open woods. Ranger Sabo arrived on the scene shortly after. The 69-year-old man was not wearing gloves or shoes, and was suffering from some frostbite on his feet and hands. He was still alert and talking.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re always looking for live people. That’s our goal is to find a live person,” mentioned Fouch. “And a lot of people are really tough. This gentleman didn’t have shoes on when we found him in the morning or mittens or gloves, so he had been out there for some period of time at night. And he still did okay. Sometimes if you keep moving in that situation, you generate enough heat to do okay.”.

In a recent development, due to his injuries and the location off the trail, a hoist was the safest and quickest way to get him to safety. Ranger Martin used a cable to hoist him up to a helicopter, while NYSP Pilot Engle flew them to the hospital.

In addition to this coordination between hunters, the NYSP, and DEC, Fouch noted that Becky the basset hound made this happy ending possible.

“I think if the dog had not shown up at Whiteface, that gentleman definitely would have had a different outcome,” said Fouch. “It definitely would have been much harder to find him. He may not have survived the rest of the day and probably not another night. The dog definitely contributed to him being saved so quickly.”.

#121052. Industry News: How Did So Many Women Become the SNL “Sister” Character?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1009 w)

Industry News: How Did So Many Women Become the SNL “Sister” Character?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • In Saturday Night Live’s “Sister” sketch, the family’s eldercare solution is The Sister (aka The Daughter).
  • Sources indicate that as I watched this clip (over and over again, trying to understand how it could be both funny and triggering simultaneously), my eyes zoomed in on this particular screen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

In Saturday Night Live’s “Sister” sketch, the family’s eldercare solution is The Sister (aka The Daughter). In this skit, Sister drops everything going on in her life to care for Dad. What struck me was one of the quick screens that flashed, describing why women feel compelled to act in this way: "years of internalized sexism," they say, have made caregiving feel like her responsibility.

Sources indicate that as I watched this clip (over and over again, trying to understand how it could be both funny and triggering simultaneously), my eyes zoomed in on this particular screen. There are icons like a television, flag, music notes, religious symbols, and a book surrounding the female caregiver.

According to recent reports, to me, these indicators are like a recipe for how daughterhood is taught. It's not one single song, policy, television show, book, or religious text that makes a daughter feel like the default support person in a family. These are messages that accumulate over a woman's lifetime. The particulars of the influencing cultural messages differ across families and communities; and, of course, each influence trigger can also provide counter-messaging. But repeated, prolonged, non-stop ideas about who is naturally nurturing, who should sacrifice, and who is responsible for family care can begin to feel like common sense. It's like Stockholm syndrome in that it seeps into your consciousness that this treatment and behavior is natural and normal and you're the one who needs to do it.

Daughterhood doesn't just start up one day when a parent becomes ill. It is built through years of everyday interactions with our cultural influences at play. For example, a young girl (eldest sister) was praised for being responsible, asked to remember a relative’s birthday, encouraged to help a younger sibling, or expected to notice when a parent is worried. High-level cognitions and emotions that are baked into our childhood tend to stay with us. These acts can be loving and ordinary. Either the family sees this as helping or they think it's part of her personality (if they notice her care provisions at all). Over time, though, repetition teaches daughter what others expect from her within the family system (and what she can expect for her own trajectory).

According to recent reports, A 2021 review of research on unpaid family care describes socialization as role learning shaped by family, culture, modeling, and normalization. In many of the studies reviewed, daughters and daughters-in-law internalized caregiving responsibility in ways connected to gender, birth order, and marriage (McAllum et al., 2021). That indicates that women feel like they're supposed to be doing the daughtering and care work. The process of internalizing this expectation is not a single lesson. It is a decades-long apprenticeship: first watching, then helping, then becoming the person others rely on.

In a recent development, when a daughter becomes so smooth at anticipating needs, her skill and ability in this role can become obscured. She's so good at care work that the history and training that produced her competence become hidden. Relatives may say she is “just better at this,” as if a daughter's skill at anticipating and noticing are just instinct instead of practice. The more a woman does well for her family, the easier it becomes for others to step back. And because care includes so much planning, emotional attunement, and follow-through, the daughter is working and laboring and giving long before anyone calls it caregiving.

In my book, Good Daughtering, I talk about the many facets of daughtering. It's the unpaid, often invisible work of holding a family together: checking in, stepping up, and smoothing over. Eldercare can bring that work into sharp focus, but it doesn't create a need for daughtering out of thin air. By the time a crisis arrives, a daughter already understands herself as the one who notices, remembers, and responds. She's been doing it for years by this point. The crisis only makes it visible to others.

Recent findings suggest that that is why the instant activation of the SNL "Sister" character matters. While the text from her brother is sudden, the role of daughtering is not. She drops everything and gets to work. Of course, she feels like refusing makes her selfish, even when the family has never asked who else could take responsibility. Guilt can make a learned expectation feel like a personal obligation. And that's our pain point. Women must learn to sit in the tense feelings of guilt while claiming recognition for our labor.

The point is not to blame daughters for internalizing the messages around them, or to assume every family follows the same script. The big point here is to ask how this "Sister" or "Daughter" social script became so familiar. And we also need to ask: who in the family benefits when one person carries the heaviest parts of the overall load?

If daughterhood is built over time, it can also be renegotiated over time. Families can make the work of caring become visible, question the assumptions that just one specific daughter will step in and do it all, and definitely teach sons and other relatives to notice, strategy, and care without waiting to be assigned.

The SNL "Sister" sketch is funny because it compresses a very common, yearslong story into a quick two minutes. But let's not forget the bigger, more difficult question that we should be asking much earlier in life: Why does everyone think it's the daughter who will be the one to go?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a latest Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder.

Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.

If Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the organization before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company. Among its more entertaining projects was a life-sized recreation of the famous Japanese Tamiya Wild One RC dune buggy, turning a childhood remote-controlled favorite into an actual drivable electric vehicle. We’ve also covered the company’s ultra-luxurious miniature electric cars, including its stunning Bentley Blower recreation.

Now the tech giant has turned its attention to Porsche, and the result is perhaps its most impressive miniature EV yet.

There’s something I love about miniature electric cars, combining the fun of four-wheels with the right-sized (or pint-sized) magic of mini-mobility.

The Porsche 550 J is based on the original 550 Spyder, Porsche’s first purpose-built racing sports car, which debuted in 1953 and went on to become a motorsport legend.

Despite being scaled down to 80% of the original’s dimensions, the upcoming electric version still seats two adults. It weighs just 350 kg (772 lb), thanks partly to its lightweight tubular steel spaceframe and hand-formed carbon fiber bodywork.

The standard version features an 8 kW (11 hp) electric motor operating on a 48V system, providing a top speed of 40 mph (65 km/h) and a range of up to 30 miles (50 km).

It has been revealed that for those who want a bit more performance from their miniature Porsche, an optional RS Pack doubles the power to 16 kW (21 hp), increases the top speed to 50 mph (80 km/h), and extends the range to 50 miles (80 km) thanks to additional batteries. The upgrade also includes drilled disc brakes and adjustable suspension.

Sources indicate that the attention to detail goes well beyond the exterior. The car features Brembo brakes, Bilstein suspension, Continental tires, and even a wood-rimmed Nardi steering wheel, just like the original. The classic dashboard retains its three-dial layout, though the fuel gauge has been replaced with a battery meter and the original choke lever now serves as a drive mode selector.

Even the charging port is cleverly hidden beneath the chrome fuel filler cap.

The project was developed in close collaboration with Porsche over six years, with Hedley Studios gaining access to original engineering drawings, archival materials, and historic vehicles in Porsche’s museum.

Only 250 examples will be produced, with buyers able to choose historic racing liveries or custom paint finishes, including colors matching their full-sized Porsches.

In a recent development, of course, this level of craftsmanship doesn’t come cheap. Prices start at £69,500 (approximately US $91,000), before taxes and options. Orders are already open through Porsche dealers and Hedley Studios, with deliveries expected to begin in spring 2027.

That’s a lot of money for a car that’s only 80% there, but then again, this isn’t really meant to be practical transportation. It’s a collector’s piece that just happens to be electric, drivable, and capable of hitting 50 mph. When there are only 250 of these being built, the £70k price is really just the entry ticket to a special, ultra-luxury club of electric mini-Porsches.

According to recent reports, and if you ask me, that sounds like a pretty fun combination. I don’t think I’ll ever be in the market for one of these personally, but I’d sure love to be friends with someone who is!

Normally, Waymo offers freeway service in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami, and Austin. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” California DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman noted to the Associated Press. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present.”.
